title: How Automation Supports Industrial Sustainability
summary: Automation and sustainability go hand in hand. Let's explore how it enables industries to modernize their processes, minimize waste, and use less energy.
body_text: In the race to fend off the most disastrous impacts of climate change, sustainability has become more than just a buzzword — it’s a guiding principle for businesses that want to remain competitive while reducing their environmental footprint. In 2023, more than 80% of the energy humanity consumed was fossil fuels, with manufacturing and its related value chains accounting for nearly 30% of global greenhouse gas emissions . These stats not only highlight the negative environmental impact of these industries but also their critical role in achieving net-zero emissions by 2050. To meet this goal, the industry must urgently adopt alternative fuels or significantly scale up carbon capture efforts. The good news is that sustainability trends in the industry are heading in the right direction. More than 8,000 companies and countries representing 90% of the global GDP have committed to reaching net zero by 2050. In addition, 59% of companies increased their energy efficiency in 2023. At Cyngn, we talk a lot about the benefits of industrial automation. The efficiency gains and safety improvements offered by our autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) alone are more than enough to justify an investment in automation. However, we have yet to explore the positive impact that driverless vehicles can have on industrial sustainability. In short, automation and green initiatives go hand in hand, allowing industries to modernize their processes, minimize waste, and use less energy. From manufacturing to logistics, industries that embrace automation are not just improving productivity— they’re also paving the way for a more sustainable future. In fact, companies that prioritize environmental sustainability not only reduce their environmental footprint but also build long-term resilience. These initiatives can improve brand reputation, attract eco-conscious customers, and generate substantial cost savings through more efficient resource use. Table of Contents Table of Contents How Automation Improves Sustainability Automation and sustainability go hand in hand. By streamlining operations and minimizing waste, automation reduces resource consumption and operational inefficiencies. Additionally, automation can lower emissions by optimizing transportation routes and reducing idle time. In fact, a study by Gecko Robotics and Rho Impact found that better use of advanced robotics and AI could result in an impressive reduction of 853 million metric tons (MMT) of CO2 annually by 2030, which is equivalent to 18% of U.S. CO2 emissions. This shift to robotics is particularly crucial for industries that rely heavily on fossil fuels or face regulatory pressures to reduce their carbon footprint. Whether it’s through electric vehicles (EVs), automated guided vehicles (AGVs), or implementations of intelligent design, automation helps lower emissions and optimize resource use across sectors. Role of Automation in Industrial Modernization Automation is at the core of Industry 4.0, where advanced robotics, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) , and artificial intelligence (AI) are reshaping industries. By optimizing workflows, minimizing downtime, and enabling real-time data collection, automation enhances industrial productivity. These technologies help companies track and reduce their environmental impact, improve labor productivity, and foster a sustainable production environment. Manufacturing Manufacturing automation improves sustainability by reducing energy consumption and waste through optimized processes and efficient resource management. A prime example of a manufacturer that turned to automation to drive sustainability is Advanced Composite Structure . By automating their production processes and utilizing lean manufacturing techniques, they were able to reduce excess raw material usage and drive workflow efficiency. As a result, they were able to boost production from 20 to 45 units per shift while cutting scrap rates from 24% to just 1.8%. Additionally, the company reduced its facility size by 73%, resulting in lower energy consumption and a significant decrease in its environmental footprint. Mining The mining industry , which has long held a reputation for being environmentally damaging, is greatly benefiting from automation through conveyance and robotic process automation (RPA). These advanced technologies are improving resource management and reducing the environmental footprint of mining operations by minimizing fuel consumption, decreasing emissions, and optimizing extraction processes. A great example of this occurred at a copper mine in Northern Chile. There, mining company Coldelco installed an 8-mile conveyance system. The belt did the work of approximately 120 long-haul trucks and reduced CO2 emissions by 70% . Coldelco isn't the only company replacing trucks with conveyance. Alamos Gold also switched to conveyance and in doing so, they were able to reduce their rate of emissions intensity (a measure of emissions per ton of material extracted) by half . Healthcare Johnson & Johnson and Novartis have both integrated automation to enhance sustainability and efficiency. Johnson & Johnson uses an AI-powered system to monitor production in real time, reducing energy use and waste, which lowers its carbon footprint. Novartis applies AI in drug development to analyze large datasets and predict outcomes, helping streamline R&D, reduce material waste, and prevent unnecessary pharmaceutical waste. Additionally, automation in supply chain management ensures that medical supplies are efficiently tracked and utilized, minimizing excess waste. These efforts highlight how automation and AI in healthcare and pharmaceuticals are improving operational efficiency while promoting sustainability. OEMs Original equipment manufacturers ( OEMs ) are also embracing automation to boost sustainability. For example, Ford, Toyota, and other leading car manufacturers have already implemented a variety of automation systems to improve their manufacturing processes and increase sustainability. BMW’s Leipzig factory embarked on a major initiative to install automated technologies to enable the recovery of materials like plastics, steel, and aluminum. This has enabled BMW to reuse more than 70% of the materials in the production process. Logistics Logistics companies are leveraging warehouse automation to drive sustainability by optimizing operations and reducing waste. As part of this warehouse transformation, AI-powered route optimization tools can reduce emissions and fuel costs, contributing to the decarbonization of logistics, which currently accounts for 24% of global CO2 emissions . Autonomous electric vehicles, such as Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) and Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs), are also playing a significant role, with companies like DHL aiming for 60% of their last-mile fleet to be electric by 2030. Additionally, warehouse automation improves inventory management, reducing excess waste and preventing overstocking, while significantly enhancing warehouse efficiency. As businesses adopt automated robots and other solutions, they not only support sustainability but also respond to consumer demand, with 66% of customers considering sustainability in their purchasing decisions. These technologies ultimately boost operational efficiency while lowering environmental impact. Sustainable Industrial Practices Digital Transformation As companies undergo digital transformation, automation enables the adoption of sustainable industrial practices. By leveraging robotic process automation (RPA), teledriving, and other digital tools, industries can achieve significant waste reduction. Teleoperations , for example, allow operators to remotely control machinery or vehicles, reducing the need for on-site personnel and minimizing transportation emissions. This technology also supports more efficient workflows by allowing operators to manage multiple locations simultaneously from a central hub. Additionally, intelligent design further minimizes unnecessary resource use, while transparency in sustainability efforts helps companies track and report their environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance​. A 2022 study found that digital transformation significantly reduces waste gas and wastewater emissions in firms, particularly in state-owned enterprises, high-polluting industries, and economically developed regions. The study identified that this reduction is driven by increased total factor productivity, green innovation, and improved internal controls. These findings suggest that digital transformation plays a crucial role in reducing corporate emissions and enhancing sustainability efforts. Robotic Process Automation Robotic Process Automation (RPA) directly supports sustainability efforts by automating repetitive and time-consuming environmental and operational tasks. For example, RPA reduces a company's carbon footprint by automating manual, energy-intensive processes like data entry, cutting down the need for physical resources such as paper and reducing greenhouse gas emissions from office equipment. In fact, according to a study from last year, 79% of respondents who deployed RPA found it to be the most effective tool for advancing their sustainability strategy. RPA can also streamline sustainability reporting by automating the collection and processing of emissions data from multiple sources, ensuring accurate and consistent environmental reporting. Additionally, in waste management, RPA tracks and segregates waste, automates recycling logistics, and ensures timely disposal processes, minimizing errors and inefficiencies that contribute to environmental harm. Moreover, in supply chain management, RPA can automate vendor assessments based on sustainability criteria, improving green procurement and reducing excess inventory, which leads to less waste and supply chain sustainability. Waste Reduction A notable example of automation reducing waste in manufacturing is Apple’s iPhone recycling robot, Daisy . Daisy can dismantle 200 iPhones per hour with precision, far exceeding human capabilities, and efficiently recover valuable materials like precious metals that would otherwise be discarded. By freezing adhesives and using innovative disassembly techniques, Daisy enhances recycling efficiency and contributes to resource conservation by reducing the need for new raw materials. This automation supports Apple's circular economy goals by reusing materials from old products in new ones, promoting sustainable manufacturing in the electronics industry. Similarly, companies like Dell and HP are leveraging automated processes in their recycling programs to recover and reuse materials, further advancing sustainability in the sector. Efficient Design and Workflows Efficient design and workflows contribute to sustainable industrial practices by minimizing resource consumption, reducing waste, and lowering energy use. A prominent example is Perkins & Will, an architecture firm leading the industry in sustainable industrial development . Their approach integrates sustainable practices at each stage, including non-toxic materials, energy-efficient systems, and biophilic design. They have committed to eliminating embodied carbon from all commercial interior spaces by 2030, achieving carbon neutrality by 2022, and targeting net-zero operational carbon for all active projects by 2030. This commitment to efficiency and sustainability demonstrates how optimized workflows can significantly reduce environmental impact. Transparency in Sustainability Transparency in sustainability is crucial for building trust with consumers and stakeholders. Automation facilitates better data collection and analytics, allowing businesses to measure their sustainability efforts more effectively. For example, with digital twins, energy monitoring, and emissions testing, companies can gain real-time insights into their environmental footprint and make more informed decisions to improve their sustainability practices. As a result, companies can also better communicate their environmental practices, demonstrating accountability and commitment to sustainable initiatives. This transparency allows customers to make informed choices and supports a shift towards more responsible consumption. In fact, research shows that 66% of consumers are willing to pay more for sustainable brands. Benefits of Bringing Sustainability to Your Operations Investing in sustainable automation brings several benefits, including: Better Labor Efficiency In manufacturing alone, 2.1 million jobs could go unfilled by 2030. Fortunately, automation improves labor efficiency by handling repetitive tasks, allowing workers to focus on higher-value activities​. This shift not only improves productivity but also boosts employee morale, as a sustainable workplace often leads to a safer and more comfortable environment. Predictive Maintenance According to a GE Digital study, predictive maintenance can reduce reactive maintenance by up to 40% . By automating predictive maintenance, companies can avoid costly breakdowns and maintenance costs, extending the lifespan of their machinery and reducing waste. Predictive maintenance further “stacks” the efficiency gains by leveraging resource-efficient machinery. Increased Revenue Sustainable practices often lead to cost savings through energy efficiency and waste reduction, boosting overall revenue. According to a report by DNV , 40% of businesses have seen revenue growth from investments in supply chain sustainability. Plus, in some cases, they can also impact revenue by attracting eco-conscious customers and enhancing brand loyalty. Environmental Benefits Automated systems reduce emissions, energy consumption, and material waste, helping companies achieve their environmental sustainability goals. This leads to a happier, healthier workforce. In the U.S., more than $820 billion is incurred each year for hospitalizations, injuries, medical treatments, mental health conditions, and lost wages linked to air pollution and climate change. Investments in sustainability can help reduce these costs and improve health outcomes. Improved Analytics Analytics can be a powerful tool for promoting sustainable and environmentally friendly industrial practices by enabling real-time monitoring, supply chain optimization, and decision-making that reduce environmental impact. For example, Unilever has made data analytics central to its sustainability strategy as part of its goal to make all products sustainable by 2030. By using analytics to track water and energy consumption, Unilever identifies areas of inefficiency, optimizes resource usage, and monitors progress toward sustainability goals. This data-driven approach allows Unilever to reduce waste, conserve water, and improve energy efficiency across its operations, demonstrating how leveraging analytics can drive meaningful environmental improvements and help industries meet ambitious sustainability targets. Bring Sustainability to Your Operations with Cyngn Are you meeting your sustainability goals? One way to tap into automation and bring sustainability to your operations is through Cyngn's autonomous solutions . With Cyngn’s fleet of AMRs, sustainability becomes a seamless part of your daily operations. Our DriveMod-enabled vehicles—including the DriveMod Tugger , the DriveMod Forklift , and the DriveMod Stockchaser —are designed to boost efficiency and safety, which alone justifies an investment in the technology. However, they also actively support your green initiatives. By optimizing workflows, our AI-powered autonomous industrial vehicles help minimize energy consumption and waste, leading to significant cost savings and a reduced carbon footprint. Frequently Asked Questions What are the benefits of prioritizing sustainability in manufacturing Prioritizing sustainability in manufacturing leads to reduced environmental impact through lower emissions and resource consumption. It improves operational efficiency by optimizing workflows and minimizing waste, which can result in significant cost savings. Sustainable practices also enhance brand reputation, attract eco-conscious customers, and build long-term business resilience. Additionally, sustainable manufacturing companies boost labor efficiency and contribute to achieving environmental goals such as reduced carbon footprints. Is automation sustainable? Yes, automation can be highly sustainable. By optimizing resource use, reducing waste, and minimizing energy consumption, automation helps industries lower their environmental footprint. Technologies like self-driving vehicles, AI, and robotic systems contribute to more efficient workflows, which reduce emissions and improve sustainability. Additionally, automation supports sustainable practices in areas such as predictive maintenance and intelligent design, further promoting eco-friendly industrial operations. What is the role of automation in environmental sustainability initiatives? Automation plays a crucial role in environmental sustainability initiatives by improving efficiency and reducing waste. Through digital transformation, technologies like robotic process automation (RPA) and teleoperations minimize resource use and emissions while streamlining workflows. For example, automated waste management systems improve recycling processes, and efficient design helps conserve energy and materials. Automation also enhances transparency, enabling better tracking and reporting of sustainability efforts, which builds trust with consumers and stakeholders.

title: How to Make AI Agents Safer
summary: Customizable AI agents have massive potential, but they also come with risks. These are some things to keep in mind at the application layer.
body_text: How to Make AI Agents Safer personal AI ai agents community Oct 24, 2024 Saba Imran As an application, Khoj helps people do better research with AI agents that can retrieve any publicly available information, read from your knowledge base, and perform some tasks on your behalf. Most of our use cases are centered around helping people learn, understand, and create. You can find all public agents here: https://app.khoj.dev/agents . Custom agent creation is currently limited to the Futurist tier . Customization is a necessity for any research utility. You’ll find yourself often wanting to tweak the agent’s behavior to better suit your needs. This could be changing the system prompt, defining the capabilities of the agent, changing what information it has access to. You can create a coding agent that specializes in Rust, a outdoorsy travel planning agent for Kyrgyzstan, a study buddy that helps you with applied linear algebra, or a creative partner that helps update the copy for your marketing campaign. You always have the general-purpose Khoj agent available, but we recognize that deeper projects require specialization. We’re really psyched to see what people come up with here. We’ve made custom agents very easy to share, because distributing knowledge and expertise amongst each other should be trivial. Currently, you can share your “protected” agents with a direct link. Once we’re more confident in the safety of the system, we’ll allow you to share your agents publicly. That being said, ease of sharing also demands increased guardrails. We’re acutely aware of the dangers that come with viral systems in the AI economy. That’s why we’ve baked a few safety features into Khoj: Prompt verification : When you save your custom protected or public agent, we’ll verify that the system prompt is responsible and abides by our community guidelines. Our agents will not support propagation of hate speech, misinformation, or any other harmful content. Prompt transparency : Anyone you share your agent with can see the system prompt you’ve configured. Transparency is critical to making sure all parties are aware of the goal function of the technology they’re interacting with. Manual agent review : When you share your agent with the world, we’ll review it to make sure it’s safe for everyone. With all that said, these principles will not be perfect. We’re constantly iterating on how to make Khoj a safer place for everyone. If you have any suggestions, please reach out to us.

body_text: At Enerflex, we are proud to have a team of dedicated experts committed to building a better energy future. Driven by their passion, they are constantly seeking innovative solutions to tackle the industry’s greatest challenges. One area we are focused on is the Permian Basin. As there are resources left to produce in the Permian, the industry is reporting an increased gas-to-oil ratio and an increased amount of CO2 in the associated gas. Tim Oneal – Lead Process Engineer for New Product Development in the USA, delved into how Enerflex can help our client partners navigate the challenges of producing in the Basin at the recent 2024 GPA Midstream Convention in San Antonio. Tim shared his insights on whether operators should remove the bulk of water with a TEG system and polish it with a small molecular sieve system or if they should invest for a fully-saturated mole sieve system and forego the TEG system altogether. His presentation ignited thought-provoking discussions and evoked inspiring insights on how we can collaborate to address this. title: The Best Examples of Data Visualization in 11 Leading Design Systems
summary: Explore how the top design systems use data visualization to create clear, accessible, and actionable insights. Learn key features and best practices for effective data presentation.
body_text: In a world driven by data, the ability to present information clearly and effectively is more critical than ever. For many companies, this challenge is solved through data visualizations embedded in their digital products. However, achieving consistency, accessibility, and usability across various platforms is no small feat, especially when it comes to visualizing complex data. This is where design systems come into play, offering a unified framework that governs not only the visual style but also the interaction and behavior of data visualizations. Whether it’s color palettes for charts, choosing the right graph types, or ensuring accessibility for all users, these systems have refined their approaches to make data both beautiful and actionable. Below, we explore some of the best examples of data visualization practices within the most advanced design systems today, showcasing live examples where possible to highlight their impact on user experience. We chose these companies as references because they regularly handle large volumes of data, making their data visualization practices critical to their products' success. Visma’s Unified Design (VUD) system Visma’s Unified Design (VUD) system serves a suite of enterprise products that rely heavily on data visualizations to communicate critical information, such as financial reports and performance analytics. As a provider of software solutions for industries like accounting, payroll, and procurement, Visma’s design system focuses on helping users make informed decisions by presenting complex data in a clear, accessible way. Key features: Limited number of colors : Visma emphasizes the use of fewer colors to ensure visualizations are accessible and easy to interpret, preventing unnecessary complexity. Differentiated by shapes and lines : By varying shapes, line thicknesses, and other visual elements in charts, Visma improves clarity, especially for users with visual impairments. Interactive visual feedback : Interactive visual feedback ensures that users can easily engage with the data, helping them understand and act on the information presented. Visma’s data visualization guidelines Datadog’s DRUIDS design system As a company focused on monitoring and analyzing massive amounts of data in real time, Datadog’s data visualizations are at the core of its platform. Their DRUIDS design system provides flexible and customizable components that empower users to monitor system performance, security metrics, and logs in real time. With data playing a central role in Datadog’s offerings, their visualizations are critical to helping users make fast, informed decisions. Key features: Change graphs : Datadog’s design system includes highly flexible change graphs, which highlight changes between two values with color-coded backgrounds. This is especially useful for tracking real-time data changes. Heatmaps and timeseries : To handle large datasets and time-based metrics, Datadog provides heatmaps and customizable timeseries charts, allowing users to visualize data trends and relationships over time. Topology maps : For network and system monitoring, Datadog includes topology maps that visualize relationships between nodes, helping users understand complex data connections at a glance. Datadog’s data visualization guidelines Atlassian’s design system Atlassian is known for its tools like Jira and Confluence, which generate vast amounts of data that teams rely on to manage tasks and workflows. The Atlassian design system provides detailed guidance on how to use color in data visualizations, ensuring that complex information is easy to interpret and accessible to all users. Key features: Single-color charts : For simplicity and clarity, Atlassian recommends using a single brand color with neutral tones, making important data stand out. Categorical colors : For different data categories, Atlassian allows up to five or six distinct colors, ensuring readability while maintaining clarity. Status and severity : Colors are also used to convey status (success, warning, danger), but Atlassian ensures that these are complemented by other visual indicators to enhance accessibility. Atlassian’s data visualization guidelines IBM’s Carbon design system IBM’s Carbon Design System offers a wide range of charts, each suited for specific types of data analysis. This design system is particularly useful for teams dealing with various data visualization needs, from comparing data to analyzing trends. Carbon excels at offering diverse chart types based on different data-driven scenarios, making it a strong reference for businesses managing a large amount of data. Key features: Extensive web platform support : Carbon’s data visualizations support vanilla JavaScript, Svelte, React, Vue and Angular. Heavily customizable charts : Chart components are highly customizable with advanced functionality such as themes, dual axes, color palettes, combo charts, and event handling. Establishes a strong hierarchy : Carbon encourages users to apply a strong hierarchy when it comes to dashboards–prioritizing data by importance. IBM Carbon’s data visualization guidelines Mailchimp’s Pattern Library Mailchimp’s platform is deeply rooted in marketing analytics, where the clear presentation of engagement and audience metrics is critical for its users. Mailchimp's pattern library provides precise guidance for designing simple, yet effective, data visualizations that are focused on helping users make quick, informed decisions. Key features: Clear charts : Mailchimp avoids decorative elements, keeping charts clean and to the point. line charts feature solid lines for actual data, with dotted lines for averages or projections, ensuring clarity. Predefined color palettes : Predefined color combinations are used to maintain visual harmony and accessibility. Mailchimp prioritizes contrast and hue variety to ensure charts are readable. Avoid pie charts : Mailchimp advises against pie charts, suggesting percent bar graphs for improved data comprehension. Mailchimp’s data visualization guidelines Shopify’s Polaris design system Shopify’s Polaris Design System provides comprehensive guidelines for data visualizations that focus on clarity and answering specific business questions. With e-commerce at its core, Shopify’s users interact with a lot of data related to sales, customer behavior, and inventory, making their design system’s data visualizations essential for day-to-day decision-making. Key features: Focused on a single question : Each visualization should answer a specific question, such as “What are my sales over time?” This keeps the visualizations simple and focused. Uses five core traits : Shopify emphasizes accuracy, intuitiveness, engagement, focus, and granularity in their data visualizations, ensuring that users get the insights they need at a glance. Axis and labeling guidelines : Axis lines and labels are designed for clarity without clutter, and color is used thoughtfully to enhance accessibility. Shopify Polaris’ data visualization guidelines Red Hat’s PatternFly design system Red Hat’s open source design system PatternFly is used for enterprise applications that require highly functional and flexible data visualizations. It offers an extensive selection of charts and best practices for designing data visualizations that prioritize clarity, usability, and interaction. Key features: Chart variety : PatternFly offers a range of chart types including area, bar, line, and pie charts, as well as more specialized charts like bullet and sparkline charts. Interactive legends : Interactive chart legends allow users to isolate or highlight specific datasets, making large and complex charts more navigable. Design elements : Consistency in elements like title alignment, tooltips, and legends helps ensure that even complex charts remain user-friendly. PatternFly’s data visualization guidelines Sprout Social’s Seeds design system Sprout Social’s platform is centered around social media analytics, where data visualizations play a critical role in helping marketers track engagement and performance metrics. Sprout Social’s Seeds design system provides clear guidelines for creating visualizations that make it easy for users to draw insights from their data. Key features: Social media performance tracking : Seeds offers charts specifically designed for tracking audience engagement and campaign performance, focusing on making trends easy to interpret. Clarity through color : The design system emphasizes the use of color to highlight key data points without overwhelming the user. Data storytelling : The system encourages the use of visualizations to tell a story, helping users make sense of complex data through clear, concise graphics. Sprout Social’s data visualization guidelines GitLab’s Pajamas design system GitLab’s Pajamas Design System provides detailed guidance on how to present data effectively, with a strong focus on turning data into actionable narratives. Given GitLab’s focus on DevOps and collaboration tools, their data visualizations aim to provide clarity and insight for users managing code, tasks, and performance. Key features: Cohesion, structure, and readability : Visualizations are designed with clear structures, making them easy to interpret. Cohesion between elements ensures that users can quickly digest complex information. Prioritizes cognition : Visualizations that align data points on a common scale are favored, as they are easier for users to interpret. The system discourages the use of pie charts, opting for visualizations that provide greater accuracy. Tailored visualization types : Pajamas breaks down visualizations into categories like hierarchical (treemaps), relational (network diagrams), and temporal (timelines) to match specific use cases. GitLab’s data visualization guidelines Orange design system The Orange design system supports the telecommunications giant’s wide range of digital products by providing clear guidelines for data visualization. Given Orange’s focus on communication services and user interaction, their design system emphasizes clarity and accessibility across platforms. Key features: Consistency across platforms : Orange’s system uses design tokens and components (for labels, text, and colors) to ensure that data visualizations look consistent across web, iOS, Android, and more, making it easy to scale visuals for different platforms. Accessibility focus : The guidelines emphasize creating data visualizations that are accessible to all users, incorporating principles like high contrast and simple labeling. Appropriate chart selection : The system guides users toward choosing the right chart type for the data being displayed, prioritizing ease of understanding. Orange’s data display guidelines Twilio’s Paste design system Twilio’s Paste Design System supports its communication APIs by offering clear guidelines on how to visualize data effectively. With Twilio handling real-time communications and large datasets, the system emphasizes visualizations that are both clear and responsive. Key features: Data simplicity : Paste emphasizes simplicity in data visualizations, ensuring that users can quickly understand data points without unnecessary complexity. Consistency with design language : The system promotes the use of Twilio’s design language to ensure that visualizations feel cohesive across different products. Customizable components : Twilio’s data visualizations are designed to be highly customizable, allowing teams to tailor visualizations to fit the specific needs of different use cases, such as real-time messaging data or API performance metrics. Twilio Paste’s data visualization guidelines These design systems represent the best practices in data visualization, each tailored to the unique needs of their respective industries. Whether it’s real-time monitoring, marketing analytics, or e-commerce data, these companies showcase how thoughtful data visualization enhances the user experience while making data more accessible and actionable.
